mainTopic: Slaughtering חולין in the עזרה and the four-or-five payment; עדים זוממין in theft cases; when an עד זומם becomes disqualified
overview: The amud opens in the middle of an argument over whether the ban on benefiting from חולין שנשחטו בעזרה is from the Torah or only דרבנן. Someone tried to prove it is only דרבנן from our משנה, which makes a thief who slaughtered in the עזרה pay four or five. רב אחא בריה דרבא pushes back, but רב אשי rejects his answer because "וּטְבָחוֹ" requires a complete slaughter. רב אשי then answers in the name of רב גמדא, quoting רבא: the thief began cutting the סימנים outside and finished inside, so the animal becomes forbidden only as the slaughter is completed. A new משנה follows about עדים זוממין who testified that someone stole an animal and then slaughtered or sold it. It explains who pays what when one pair or two pairs of witnesses are proven false, and why the whole case falls if a theft witness is false. The גמרא then brings a dispute: אביי says an עד זומם is disqualified going backward, from when he testified, and רבא says only from when he is caught. A second version says רבא really agrees with אביי, and his different reason continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why the משנה seems to show the ban is only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: If the ban on חולין slaughtered in the עזרה were from the Torah, the animal would become forbidden at the first bit of slaughter. The thief would then not be slaughtering the owner's animal, so he should not have to pay four or five.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if you think this ban is from the Torah, then as soon as he slaughters the animal a little, he has made it forbidden. For the rest of the slaughter, it is no longer the owner's animal that he is slaughtering!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning behind a proof made just before this section. The proof is that the ban on חולין בעזרה is not דאורייתא, because our משנה makes the thief pay תשלומי ארבעה וחמשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal that is אסור בהנאה (forbidden for any benefit) is worthless to its owner, so it no longer really counts as 'his.' If the תורה forbids it from the first cut, then the rest of the slaughter is done on a forbidden animal. The תורה's four-or-five payment requires slaughtering the owner's animal, so the משנה would make no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: If it enters your mind (if you think that)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the start of the discussion. It is the reasoning for a proof made just before this section. The 'it' throughout is a non-sacred (חולין) animal being slaughtered inside the עזרה.

phrases.english: For if it enters your mind that it is from the Torah,
phrases.notes: 'It' means the ban on benefiting from חולין that were slaughtered in the עזרה.

phrases.english: as soon as he slaughters it a little, he has forbidden it,
so for the rest, it is not its owner's animal that he is slaughtering!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the proof made before this section, explaining why the משנה implies the ban is only דרבנן.
steps.raayaObject: That the ban on benefiting from חולין שנשחטו בעזרה is not דאורייתא
steps.raayaSupportSource: Our משנה, which obligates a thief who slaughtered חולין in the עזרה to pay תשלומי ארבעה וחמשה

steps.title: The thief is liable for that first bit of slaughter
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא answers that even if the ban is from the Torah, the thief's liability comes from that first small part of the slaughter, before the animal became forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא, the son of רבא, said to him: When the thief becomes obligated, it is also for that first little bit.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בריה דרבא pushes back on the proof. He says the משנה can work even if the ban is דאורייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the first small cut, the animal still belonged to the owner. רב אחא says the obligation to pay four or five is tied to that first moment, so it does not matter that the animal became forbidden afterward.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Acha, son of Rava, said to him:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי קָא מִחַיַּיב נָמֵי – אַהָהוּא פּוּרְתָּא.
phrases.english: When he becomes obligated, it is also for that little bit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 1 by placing the liability at the first moment of slaughter.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the משנה proves the ban is only דרבנן
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumes liability depends on the whole slaughter; it could instead come from the first bit, before the animal became forbidden.

steps.title: The verse requires a complete slaughter
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says this answer does not work. The פסוק "וּטְבָחוֹ" requires slaughtering the whole animal, and a little bit of slaughter is not that.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to him: Do not push the proof aside this way. The verse says "and slaughters it", which means we need the whole slaughter, and that is missing here.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי rejects רב אחא's answer, which brings the original proof back to life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה's word "וּטְבָחוֹ" means a full, complete slaughter. A first small cut is not a slaughter at all, so the thief cannot become liable for it. That puts the liability back at the end of the slaughter, when the animal is already forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not push it aside (do not reject the proof this way)
All of it, the whole thing
And there is not (it is missing)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule that liability for four or five requires a complete slaughter, which shapes the final answer.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי: לָא תִּידְחֲיַהּ,
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to him: Do not push it aside,
phrases.notes: He means: don't knock down the proof with that answer.

phrases.english: "And slaughters it": we need all of it, and it is not there.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי: לָא תִּידְחֲיַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב אחא's answer from step 2, restoring the proof of step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב אחא's claim that liability comes from the first bit of slaughter
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק "וּטְבָחוֹ" requires a complete slaughter, so a first small cut cannot create liability.

steps.title: Then the משנה is difficult again
steps.stepSummary: Since liability needs a full slaughter, the משנה again seems impossible if the ban is from the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then the משנה is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The other side now presses רב אשי: if you are right, how can the משנה make the thief pay four or five? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two ideas now clash. A full slaughter is required, yet the animal becomes forbidden from the first cut if the ban is דאורייתא. So it looks like the thief never fully slaughters the owner's animal.

phrases.english: But then it is difficult!
phrases.notes: The problem is our משנה, which makes the thief pay four or five for slaughtering חולין in the עזרה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from step 3: once רב אחא's answer is gone, the משנה is a problem again.
steps.kashyaTarget: How the משנה can obligate the thief if the ban on חולין בעזרה is דאורייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A full slaughter is needed, but the animal is forbidden from the first cut, so the thief never fully slaughters the owner's animal.

steps.title: He started outside and finished inside
steps.stepSummary: Quoting רב גמדא in the name of רבא, רב אשי answers that the משנה describes a thief who cut part of the סימנים outside the עזרה and finished inside. The animal becomes forbidden only at the very end, at the same moment the slaughter is complete.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what רב גמדא said in the name of רבא. When is the thief obligated? For example, where he slaughtered part of the סימנים outside and finished them inside.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the difficulty by narrowing the case in the משנה to a specific situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Part of the slaughter happened outside the עזרה, where no ban applies, so the animal stayed the owner's. The slaughter was finished inside. The animal becomes forbidden and the slaughter becomes complete at the same moment, so the thief is liable even if the ban is דאורייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: The windpipe and food pipe that are cut in שחיטה

steps.whatToRemember: Even if the ban on חולין בעזרה is דאורייתא, the משנה works in a case where the thief began the slaughter outside the עזרה and finished it inside. So the משנה does not prove the ban is only rabbinic.
steps.whyThisMatters: This removes the proof that the ban is only דרבנן. Our משנה can fit even the view that it is from the Torah.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, הָכִי אָמַר רַב גַּמָּדָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא:
phrases.english: He said to him: This is what Rav Gamda said in the name of Rava:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי קָא מְחַיֵּיב – כְּגוֹן שֶׁשָּׁחַט מִקְצָת סִימָנִין בַּחוּץ,
phrases.english: When is he obligated? For example, where he slaughtered part of the simanim outside,
phrases.notes: Outside means outside the עזרה, the Temple courtyard.

phrases.english: and finished them inside.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, הָכִי אָמַר רַב גַּמָּדָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty of step 4 by setting the משנה in a specific case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to describe a slaughter done entirely inside the עזרה, which would make it impossible if the ban is דאורייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה describes a slaughter begun outside and finished inside, so the animal becomes forbidden only as the slaughter is completed.

steps.title: New משנה: false witnesses about theft and slaughter
steps.stepSummary: If two witnesses testify that someone stole an animal and then slaughtered or sold it, and they are found to be עדים זוממין, the witnesses pay the full amount, including the four or five payment.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If a person stole according to two witnesses, and slaughtered or sold according to the same witnesses, and they were found to be זוממין, they pay everything.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It rules that עדים זוממין in a theft case pay everything they tried to make the accused pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עדים זוממין are punished with whatever they tried to do to the accused (כאשר זמם). They tried to make him pay four or five times the animal's value, which already includes the principal and the double payment, so they must pay that full amount themselves.

keyTerms.meaning: According to (the testimony of) two witnesses
Plotting false witnesses, proven false by other witnesses

steps.confusionAlert: 'They pay' means the false witnesses pay, not the accused thief.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: He stole, according to two witnesses,
and slaughtered or sold it, according to them,
and they were found to be zomemim: they pay everything.
phrases.notes: 'Everything' means the full four or five payment, not just the value of the animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic: עדים זוממין in a theft case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עדים זוממין who testified about theft and slaughter or sale pay the full amount, including the four or five payment.

steps.title: Two sets of witnesses, both caught lying
steps.stepSummary: When one pair of witnesses testifies about the theft and a different pair testifies about the slaughter or sale, and both pairs are found to be זוממין, each pair pays only for its own part.
steps.simpleTranslation: If two witnesses said he stole, and two other witnesses said he slaughtered or sold it, and both pairs turned out to be זוממין, then the first pair pays the תשלומי כפל and the second pair pays the extra three.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a new case. This time the theft and the slaughter were each proven by a different pair of witnesses, and both pairs are caught as זוממין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each pair of witnesses tried to make the accused pay a different part of the penalty. The theft witnesses would have made him pay double, so they pay the double. The slaughter witnesses would have made him pay the extra amount above the double, so they pay that extra.

keyTerms.meaning: Witnesses proven false because other witnesses say they were somewhere else at the time
The double payment a thief pays
The extra three payments, on top of the double, for slaughtering or selling a stolen ox
The first pair of witnesses and the last pair of witnesses

steps.confusionAlert: The second pair does not pay four or five. They pay only the extra part, because the double payment is already covered by the first pair.

phrases.english: If he stole, according to two witnesses,

phrases.aramaic: וְטָבַח וּמָכַר עַל פִּי שְׁנַיִם אֲחֵרִים,
phrases.english: and slaughtered or sold, according to two other witnesses,
and both these and those were found to be conspiring witnesses,
the first pair pays the double payment,
and the last pair pays the threefold payment.
phrases.notes: For an ox the total is five, so after the double there are three left. For a sheep it would be two.

steps.triggerLanguage: גָּנַב עַל פִּי שְׁנַיִם, וְטָבַח וּמָכַר עַל פִּי שְׁנַיִם אֲחֵרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands step 6's case of one pair of witnesses for everything into a case where two different pairs testify.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each pair of עדים זוממין pays the part of the penalty that their own testimony would have caused: the theft witnesses pay the double, and the slaughter or sale witnesses pay the extra amount.

steps.title: Only the second set is caught lying
steps.stepSummary: If only the slaughter or sale witnesses are caught as זוממין, the theft still stands. The thief pays double to the owner, and the lying witnesses pay the thief the extra amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: If only the last pair turned out to be זוממין, the thief still pays the double payment, and they pay the extra three.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second version of the case. Here the theft witnesses are still believed, and only the slaughter or sale witnesses are proven false.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The theft is still proven, so the thief really owes the double payment. The slaughter or sale is not proven anymore, so the false witnesses pay the extra amount they tried to take from him.

phrases.english: If the last pair were found to be conspiring witnesses,
he pays the double payment,
phrases.notes: "He" is the thief. He pays the owner because the theft is still proven.

phrases.english: and they pay the threefold payment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A variation of step 7 in which only the second pair is proven false.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When only the slaughter or sale witnesses are זוממין, the thief pays תשלומי כפל and the witnesses pay the extra amount.

steps.title: Only one witness is caught lying
steps.stepSummary: If one witness from the second pair is a זומם, only the slaughter or sale testimony falls. If one witness from the first pair is a זומם, the whole case falls, because without a theft there can be no penalty for slaughtering or selling.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one of the last witnesses is a זומם, the second testimony is cancelled. If one of the first witnesses is a זומם, all the testimony is cancelled, because if there is no theft, there is no slaughter payment and no sale payment.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now looks at cases where only one witness from a pair is caught lying, and tells us which testimony falls apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A testimony needs two good witnesses, so one false witness is enough to cancel the testimony he was part of. The slaughter and sale penalty is built on top of the theft. So if the theft testimony falls, the slaughter testimony has nothing left to stand on.
steps.whatToRemember: The slaughter or sale penalty depends completely on the theft. Cancel the theft and you cancel everything. Cancel only the slaughter testimony and the theft still stands.

phrases.english: If one of the last witnesses is a conspiring witness,
the second testimony is cancelled.
If one of the first witnesses is a conspiring witness,
the entire testimony is cancelled;
for if there is no theft,
there is no slaughtering and there is no selling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה's cases by moving from whole pairs being proven false to just one witness.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One false witness cancels his own pair's testimony. If that happens to the theft testimony, the slaughter or sale testimony falls too, because it depends on the theft.

steps.title: When does a lying witness become disqualified?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with a dispute. אביי says an עד זומם is disqualified going backward, from when he testified. רבא says he is disqualified only from the moment he is caught and onward.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was said about an עד זומם: אביי says he is disqualified going backward. רבא says he is disqualified from now on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins with a new question about an עד זומם: from what point in time is he no longer a valid witness? This sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees an עד זומם cannot be a witness anymore. The argument is about timing. For אביי, any testimony he gave between his lie and the moment he was caught is also cancelled. For רבא, those in-between testimonies stay valid, because he is disqualified only once he is caught.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that analyzes the משנה

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a famous dispute between אביי and רבא. It decides whether testimony he gave in between, for example at a wedding or in a court case, is still valid.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
It was stated: a conspiring witness,
Abaye said: he is disqualified retroactively,
phrases.notes: Going back to the moment he gave the false testimony.

phrases.aramaic: רָבָא אָמַר: מִכָּאן וּלְהַבָּא הוּא נִפְסָל.
phrases.english: Rava said: he is disqualified from here onward.
phrases.notes: "From here" means from when he is proven a זומם in court.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the משנה to the גמרא and starts a new topic about עדים זוממין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי: an עד זומם is disqualified retroactively from the time of his testimony. רבא: he is disqualified only from the time he is proven a זומם and onward.

steps.title: אביי's reason: the witness became wicked when he testified
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the עד זומם became a רשע at the moment he gave false testimony. The תורה says not to accept a רשע as a witness, so he is disqualified from that moment.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי says he is disqualified going backward. From the moment he gave his testimony he became a wicked person, and the תורה says: Do not make a wicked person a witness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason for אביי's view from step 10, that an עד זומם is disqualified going backward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's logic is simple. The lie happened when the witness testified, not when he was caught, so that is when he became a רשע. Getting caught only shows us what was already true.

keyTerms.meaning: A wicked person, who is not allowed to be a witness
Do not make a wicked person a witness (read from a פסוק)

steps.whyThisMatters: If he is disqualified going backward, any testimony he gave between the lie and the time he was caught is also thrown out.

phrases.english: Abaye said: he is disqualified retroactively
because from that moment that he testified
he became a wicked man
and the Torah said:
"Do not put a wicked man as a witness."
phrases.notes: שמות 23:1. The גמרא reads this פסוק to mean: never let a wicked person serve as a witness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind אביי's opinion from step 10
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עד זומם is a רשע from the moment of his false testimony, so he is disqualified from then on, which means going backward from when he is caught.

steps.title: רבא's reason: the law of עד זומם goes against normal logic
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the law of עדים זוממין is a חידוש. Logically it is two witnesses against two, so there is no reason to believe the second pair over the first. Only the תורה's special rule makes us believe them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא says he is disqualified only from now on, because the law of an עד זומם is a חידוש. Really it is two witnesses against two. What makes you listen to these? Listen to those!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason for רבא's view from step 10, that the witness is disqualified only from the time he is caught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the second pair says the first pair was somewhere else, that is really two against two, and logic says we cannot know who is lying. The תורה still tells us to believe the second pair. Since this rule does not come from logic, רבא treats it as a special rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A special rule that goes against normal logic
What did you see? (Why pick this side over that one?)

steps.confusionAlert: Here חידוש does not mean 'a new idea'. It means a rule that does not fit normal logic, so we only apply it as far as we must.

phrases.aramaic: רָבָא אָמַר מִכָּאן וּלְהַבָּא הוּא נִפְסָל –
phrases.english: Rava said: he is disqualified from now on
because a conspiring witness is a novelty
since this is two witnesses against two
What did you see that you listen to these (the second pair)?
phrases.notes: The letters in square brackets are the corrected wording, so read it as 'you listen'.

phrases.english: Listen to those (the first pair)!

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר מִכָּאן וּלְהַבָּא הוּא נִפְסָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing reason, for רבא's view, after אביי's reason
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The law of עדים זוממין is a חידוש because logically it is two against two.

steps.title: So the disqualification starts only when the special rule kicks in
steps.stepSummary: Because the law is a חידוש, we only apply it from the moment it happens, which is when the witnesses are caught, and not going backward.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore you only have him disqualified from the time of the חידוש and onward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבא's reasoning and draws the result from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rule that goes against logic is not stretched further than needed. The חידוש only takes effect at the moment of הזמה, so the disqualification also starts only then.

keyTerms.meaning: From the time of the special rule and onward

steps.whatToRemember: אביי says disqualified going backward, because he became a רשע when he lied. רבא says only from now on, because the law of עד זומם is a חידוש that starts when he is caught.

phrases.english: Therefore you have nothing with him
except from the time of the novelty and onward.
phrases.notes: The time of the חידוש means the moment the second pair of witnesses catches them.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִלְכָּךְ אֵין לְךָ בּוֹ אֶלָּא מִשְּׁעַת חִידּוּשׁ וְאֵילָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the result of רבא's reasoning from step 12
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to רבא, an עד זומם is disqualified only from the moment of הזמה and onward.

steps.title: Another version: רבא really agrees with אביי
steps.stepSummary: Some say רבא actually agrees with אביי that an עד זומם is disqualified going backward. The גמרא is about to give a different reason for רבא's ruling here.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are those who say: רבא also agrees with אביי, who said he is disqualified going backward. And here, this is רבא's reason:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of רבא's view. This line sets up the next move, and the actual reason comes in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version רבא accepts אביי's basic idea that the witness became a רשע when he lied. The question now is why רבא still does not disqualify him going backward in this case, and the גמרא is about to explain that.

phrases.english: There are those who say:
Rava also holds like Abaye
who said he is disqualified retroactively
and here, this is Rava's reason:

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי רָבָא נָמֵי כְּאַבַּיֵּי סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the version of רבא's reasoning in steps 12-13 with another version
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the second version, רבא agrees in principle that an עד זומם is disqualified going backward. His reason for ruling otherwise here comes next.
